text.p: Hawaiian Electric Industries Inc said its American Savings Bank subsidiary will record a non-recurring after-tax charge for the three months ended September 30 of about $8.3 million, or $0.27 per share.
The company said the charge is to reflect a deposit-insurance premium special assessment on thrifts by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation.
The one-time assessment was included in legislation signed into law by President Clinton on September 30, it said.
In anticipation of the assessment, the company said it infused $9 million of additional equity capital in American Savings.

Hawaiian Electric is a holding company that services the Pacific island through its electric utility, savings bank, maritime freight transportation and residential real estate development subsidiaries.
